summary: Shiitake tacos with Asian pear slaw: onion, quartered shiitakes, dry-roasted jalapeno and garlic and full-size bok choy sauteed with cinnamon and cumin, served on doubled corn tortillas with a lime, Asian pear, red onion and cilantro slaw; vegan, makes 8 tacos in 30 minutes.
glance: jalapenos and unpeeled garlic dry-roasted 5 minutes in a skillet
full-grown (10 to 12 inches, dark green leaves), not baby
faq: Why dry-roast the jalapenos and garlic?

A technique very typical in Mexican cuisine: a quick way of both mellowing and concentrating the flavors. Cook them in a hot skillet without oil for five minutes; wear disposable rubber gloves when seeding and chopping the jalapenos to avoid burning hands later.
What bok choy should I use?
The full-grown vegetable, usually about 10 to 12 inches long with dark green leaves; don't substitute baby bok choy.
How do I make the slaw?

Julienne a peeled Asian pear with a mandoline or knife, tossing frequently with the lime juice so it doesn't brown, then add thinly sliced red onion, cilantro and salt. It can be used as a condiment for other dishes, with a little toasted sesame oil for an Asian meal.
What do I serve with these tacos?
Big plates of refried beans, Mexican rice (or the non-traditional arroz verde) and homemade guacamole for a feast a bit more work than ordinary taco night.
How do I make the dish milder?
Remove the seeds and ribs of the jalapenos.

summary: Rosemary-blueberry sauce: 12 ounces of fresh blueberries simmered about 15-30 minutes with sugar, a pinch of salt and just 1/8 teaspoon of minced rosemary until between syrup and jam; makes about 1 cup, 5 minutes active, and keeps several days.
glance: 12 ounces blueberries, 1/4 cup sugar, 1/8 teaspoon minced rosemary
faq: What is it good on?
The author first made it for Manouri cheese blintzes, but it's equally amazing on vanilla ice cream, cheesecake or cornmeal pancakes.
How much rosemary?
The key is the right amount to create an interesting balance without overpowering the fruit: 1/8 teaspoon to start, and after about 15 minutes taste and add a little more if you like.
How thick should it be?
Somewhere between syrup and jam. When the berries have started to break down, dip a spoon in the sauce, let it cool, and check; if not thick enough, check again every 5 minutes.
How do I serve it?
Immediately for hot applications, or cool in the refrigerator; it keeps for several days.
Is it vegan?
Yes, it's vegan and gluten-free.

summary: Banana muffins with a crumb top, less sweet than most so you taste the banana: 3 mashed ripe bananas, brown sugar, egg and melted butter folded into flour, topped with a brown sugar and salt crumb and baked at 375°F for about 20 minutes; makes 10.
glance: 375°F for about 20 minutes, until a tester comes out dry
brown sugar crumb with flour, cinnamon, butter and flaky salt
faq: Why this recipe?
The author finds most banana muffin recipes too sweet: he wants to taste banana, not overpowering sugar. It is a composite of several recipes, borrowing the most from one at Allrecipes.
How do I keep the muffins tender?
Mix the dry and wet ingredients thoroughly and separately, then fold the dry into the wet without mixing any more than necessary. Overmixing will make them tough.
How do I make the crumb topping?

Cut 1 tablespoon of butter into 1/3 cup brown sugar (preferably something delicious like Muscovado), 2 tablespoons flour, a pinch of cinnamon and optionally a pinch or two of flaky finishing salt like pie crust, then sprinkle evenly over the batter.
How could I get more banana flavor?
The author wondered afterward whether caramelizing the bananas first, or using the smaller, intensely flavored bananas that good stores carry, would be better; he hasn't tried.
How many muffins does it make?
10, filling 10 cups of a muffin pan.

summary: Giant Dutch baby with sauteed apples: a blender batter of 5 eggs, milk and flour poured into a sizzling buttered 12-inch cast-iron skillet and baked about 18 minutes at 425°F until puffed, topped with brown sugar-cinnamon apples, powdered sugar and lemon wedges; serves 3 to 5.
glance: 425°F for about 18 minutes, until puffed and golden brown
well-seasoned 12-inch cast iron with 6 tablespoons butter heated first
2, sliced into 16 pieces each, sauteed 5 minutes then glazed with brown sugar and cinnamon
faq: What is a Dutch baby?

A giant oven-baked pancake that puffs up and then sinks in the center, to be filled with powdered sugar and fruit. It's similar to clafoutis, with a batter that has a bit less flour and more milk so it's more custardy than eggy.
Why make it for brunch?
The author thinks it could be his go-to brunch recipe: you can make the batter and the apples ahead, it finishes in the oven so you can hang out with your guests, and it's a little festive.
How do I cook it?

Put 6 tablespoons of butter in a well-seasoned 12-inch cast-iron skillet in a 425°F oven; when sizzling, pull it out and swirl to coat, pour in the blender batter (eggs, milk, flour, salt blended 1 minute) and return it to the oven for about 18 minutes.
Can I make it savory?

The batter isn't sweetened, so there's room to experiment: the author liked a savory version by Eating Out Loud and would like to try cubes of Swiss cheese and smoked paprika, or dress it up with ice cream for dessert.
How do I serve it?
Pat off excess butter, top with the apples and powdered sugar, and since it's in a really hot skillet consider serving it onto plates directly. Lemon wedges add a nice counterpoint to the sweetness.

summary: Roasted cippolini onions and beets with a sweet-and-sour agrodolce dressing: 2 pounds of cippolini and 1 pound of beets in 3/4-inch chunks tossed with olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt and sugar and roasted at 400°F for 45 minutes to an hour; vegan, serves 4, 65 minutes.
glance: 400°F, 45 minutes to 1 hour, until tender and caramelizing in spots
1/4 cup red wine vinegar, olive oil, salt, 2 teaspoons sugar
faq: What is agrodolce?
The Italian name for a slightly sweet-and-sour dressing, which elevates this simple side dish of roasted onions and beets.
What are cippolini onions?
Small, rather flat onions found at farmers markets or Italian or gourmet grocers. Don't confuse them with pearl onions, which are too small for this dish.
Can I use golden beets?
Yes, but use white wine vinegar instead of red so as not to ruin their color.
How do I prepare the vegetables?
Peel the beets and cut into roughly 3/4-inch cubes; remove a slice from the top and bottom of each onion, peel, and cut into chunks of the same size. Roast in a single layer.
How do I serve it?
Hot or warm, with a savory tart, as a garnish on couscous, or over a sharp bitter green such as escarole.

summary: Indian-Sichuan pickle: a tablespoon each of black mustard seeds and a teaspoon each of cumin and fennel seeds popped in hot oil for about a minute and tossed with a cup of chopped Sichuan preserved vegetable; vegan, 5 minutes, makes 1 cup and keeps several days.
glance: 1 cup chopped Sichuan preserved vegetable (about 2 whole knobs)
faq: What are Indian pickles?

Not well known in America but served as part of just about any meal in India: intense pickles made with anything from lime to garlic put up in mustard oil and lots of spices. A teaspoon or two adds interest to even the simplest bowl of rice and dal.
Where does this recipe come from?

The author had half a can of Sichuan preserved vegetable left from making Sichuan dry-fried green beans and tofu and realized it wouldn't take much to convert it into a condiment at home with Indian food.
How do I make it?

Heat the oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat, add the mustard, cumin and fennel seeds and cook about 1 minute until the mustard seeds pop and everything is fragrant but not burning, then toss with the preserved vegetable.
How long does it keep?
Serve right away or keep in the refrigerator for several days.
What do I serve it with?
Rice and dal, or any Indian dish such as chana mushroom masala.

summary: Tteokbokki, spicy Korean rice cake stew: frozen tteok simmered in water with kochujang, sugar, soy sauce, rice vinegar and ginger for 5 minutes, then eggplant and shiitakes added and cooked about 15 more minutes until the sauce is thick like a stew but not gummy; vegan, serves 4.
glance: 1 pound frozen tteok, any shape (check for wheat if gluten-free)
5 minutes, then about 15 more with the vegetables
3 cups water, 2 tablespoons kochujang, sugar, light soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger
faq: What is tteok?

Also transliterated ddeok or duk, a type of Korean rice cake you can buy frozen at any Korean grocer or better general Asian grocers. The two common shapes are flat ovals and cylinders about 1/4 inch in diameter, used in stir-fries and soups like the New Year's dish tteok guk.
What is kochujang?

A ubiquitous Korean paste of fermented chilis, soybeans and rice that tastes like fiery miso. After buying a small tub there are plenty of other uses: kimchi fried rice, spicy fried zucchini and kimchi stew.
How do I know when tteokbokki is done?

The most important judgment: the tteok should be tender and cooked through, but not cooked so long that they leach out tons of starch and make an overly gooey sauce. It should be thick like a stew, not a soup and not gummy and tight; add a bit more water at the end to adjust.
Can I change the vegetables?
Yes. Koreans put almost any vegetable in tteokbokki, plus hardboiled eggs, even mandu or noodles. Think about the timing so the ingredients finish together, or add precooked items at the end.
Why use a non-stick pan?
The tteok do tend to stick a bit, so check the bottom while stirring.

summary: "Rings of Saturn": donut (Saturn) peaches on challah French toast circles with a buttermilk sauce (thickened with a little xanthan gum), a marionberry jam sauce spiked with rosewater, pepper and cardamom, and dulce de leche ice cream pressed into the pit hole; serves 4.
glance: 4 donut (Saturn) peaches, cored; or halved regular peaches or nectarines
challah or brioche cut into circles bigger than the peaches, cooked over moderately low heat in butter
buttermilk with 1/8 teaspoon xanthan gum, marionberry jam with rosewater and cardamom
faq: What is a Saturn peach?
Donut peaches and Saturn peaches are the same thing. The author found them perfectly ripe and sweet but lacking the acid backbone of most other varieties: pure, addictive, three-bite candy.
What if I can't find Saturn peaches?
Use half of a regular peach or nectarine, cut in half along the equator. Peel only if the skin is kind of tough.
Why xanthan gum in the buttermilk sauce?

To thicken it enough to stand up on a plate a bit without being gelatinous. Without xanthan gum the sauce will just be a bit runny; thick Greek yogurt can replace buttermilk. Start with 1/8 teaspoon and add pinches until it's thick enough.
How do I make the marionberry sauce?

Whisk 1/2 cup marionberry jam (or another jam) with 1 teaspoon rosewater (or orange flower water), a grind of black pepper and a pinch of cardamom, then force through a sieve to remove lumps and seeds.
How should I cook the French toast?

Soak thick slices of challah or brioche well on both sides in the egg, milk, honey and salt mixture, brush off the excess and cook over moderately low heat in melted butter, flipping when golden brown. You don't want the heat so high that the outside burns before the inside sets.
Is the recipe precise?
The author didn't measure anything, so it's a rough guide.

summary: Crostini with white beans and basil: cannellini lightly mashed with olive oil, Meyer lemon juice, basil, salt and pepper and spooned onto thinly sliced baguette brushed with olive oil and toasted at 400°F until golden; vegan, serves 6 as an appetizer.
glance: one 15-ounce can cannellini, drained and rinsed (or cook your own)
juice of 1 Meyer lemon, 1/3 cup basil chiffonade, peppery olive oil
faq: Where does this topping come from?

It's the last of three crostini toppings the author made for a Kavana Men Cook event, and it is similar to his other white bean dip with grilled onions but pared down to clear flavors from the Meyer lemon and basil.
What can I add?
Garlic and/or chili flakes would be appropriate additions.
Can I use other herbs?
Yes, fresh parsley, tarragon or oregano instead of basil.
How do I make the toasts?
Slice a baguette thinly, arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet, brush with the remaining olive oil and toast in a 400°F oven until golden brown. Serve immediately.
How do I make the topping?
Lightly mash the beans and mix in 2 tablespoons of olive oil, the lemon juice, basil, salt and pepper, then adjust the seasoning.

summary: Peach and sour cream buckle, based on a Joy of Cooking recipe: a whole wheat pastry flour cake with 3 cups of sliced peaches folded in and a cinnamon streusel on top, baked at 350°F in a 9x9 pan for about 40 minutes and served warm with vanilla ice cream; serves 8.
glance: 350°F for about 40 minutes, until browned and a toothpick comes out clean
3 cups peeled and sliced (about 12 slices per peach)
faq: What is a buckle?

A cakey, sweet, soft, crumbly, moist dessert filled with fruit under a streusel topping. The author says it may not be the most lovely-looking dessert you ever baked, but it is cakey and filled with glorious peaches.
How do I make the streusel?

Mix 1/2 cup sugar, 6 tablespoons flour, cinnamon and salt, then work in 4 tablespoons of cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse cornmeal, as for pie crust. A few larger bits of butter are fine. Refrigerate until ready.
How do I mix the batter?

Beat the butter, sugar, egg and vanilla until fluffy, beat in the sour cream and milk, then gradually add the flour mixture and combine gently until just mixed, like pancake batter. Gently fold in the peaches, preferably with your hands; it will seem like way too many peaches.
How should I serve it?
Cool for 20 minutes and serve while still warm, with vanilla ice cream.
Any variations?
The author meant to use half dark brown sugar but forgot, and asks readers to report back if they do.
